result.rationale: In zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts the diff passes `credentialId` to refreshOAuthTokens as the third argument, while all other call sites (google-calendar, hubspot, lark-calendar, office365-calendar, msteams, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) pass `credential.userId`. The variable `credentialId` in BiginCalendarService is the credential row id, not a user id, yet refreshOAuthTokens sends it as `calcomUserId` in the sync payload (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), so credential-sharing deployments would sync against the wrong identifier. Real, verifiable inconsistency introduced by the diff.

judged_text: This call site passes `credentialId` as the sync request's calcomUserId while all eight other call sites pass credential.userId; credentialId in this scope is the credential row id, so sync-mode requests carry the wrong identifier. In credential-sharing deployments the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id instead of the user id and returns tokens for the wrong user (or fails), breaking Zoho Bigin sync and potentially cross-wiring tokens between users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` treats that third argument as `userId` and sends it as `calcomUserId` in the sync-mode POST body (`calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). In this file, `credentialId` is not `credential.userId` (other call sites in the diff consistently pass `credential.userId`), so in sync-mode the endpoint would receive a credential DB row id instead of the Cal.com user id, causing incorrect/failed token refresh for Zoho Bigin.
